title: NUMA & Memory Hierarchy
summary: On multi-socket machines, memory access cost depends on which CPU owns the DIMM. NUMA-aware placement of threads and buffers can dominate low-latency and high-throughput performance.

sections.title: What NUMA changes
paragraphs: Uniform memory assumptions fail on multi-socket servers. Remote memory access adds latency and reduces bandwidth. Allocators and thread schedulers that ignore locality leave performance on the table.
For trading engines, packet processing, and in-memory databases, NUMA can mean double-digit percent latency differences.

sections.title: Placement strategies
paragraphs: Pin threads to nodes; allocate memory first-touch on the same node; avoid false sharing across cache lines. Tools: numactl, hwloc, perf.
Shared structures either replicate per node or accept remote access with careful design.

sections.title: Interaction with NICs and GPUs
paragraphs: NIC IRQ affinity and GPU affinity should match the consuming CPU node. Cross-node PCIe traffic is a silent tax.

sections.title: When to care
paragraphs: Single-socket cloud VMs may hide NUMA. Bare metal and large instances expose it. Benchmark with production-like pinning.

deepDive.title: NUMA & Memory Hierarchy — Operations
paragraphs: Operating NUMA & Memory Hierarchy in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: NUMA & Memory Hierarchy — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around NUMA & Memory Hierarchy include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: NUMA & Memory Hierarchy — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, NUMA & Memory Hierarchy intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

keyTakeaways: Memory locality is a first-class design input on multi-socket hosts
Pinning + first-touch are the basic tools
whyItMatters: Low-latency and high-throughput systems often lose more to NUMA than to algorithm choice.
reflectionQuestions: Is your deployment single-socket or multi-socket in production?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
